symbols.note: copied by hand from gatekit symbols system --dll dx11 (addresses are bg3_dx11.exe). Methods with null address were listed by the Toolkit but the tool printed no game address for them. System index variable bg3_dx11.exe+0x60D9794; the game functions using the index are in the Toolkit line of the tool output. The does layer cites EoCServer.dll (Toolkit pseudo-code with real names) wherever bg3_dx11.exe functions were not individually mapped.
symbols.limits: reads/writes: the component views in the parameters of the system's exported methods. uses: the component operations (add, remove, get, has) its per-frame update performs through the engine's out-of-line helpers, itself or in a function it calls (depth 2), with the call site; kind index: a matched method reads the type's index and the operation is not known. Not listed: operations the compiler inlined, those deeper than depth 2, and what a method that is not the update does (e.g. a SystemLoad) - read its pseudo-code; an empty writes list is not "writes nothing".

does.text: Queues (entity, eoc::inventory::ELockChange) in a map at this+0x10; a later request for the same entity overwrites the earlier one. The client side sends the same request (ecl::inventory::ProtocolRequestSystem::LEGACY_RequestLockInventories, eocnet LockMessageData), so it comes from a player's UI action.

does.text: For each queued entity that is valid and has eoc::inventory::OwnerComponent, it reads whether it already has eoc::inventory::IsLockedComponent. Change 0: when not locked and the entity has eoc::PlayerComponent, adds IsLockedComponent. Change 1: when locked, removes it. Change 2 toggles: locked -> removed; not locked -> added under the same PlayerComponent condition. Then the queue is cleared. The component goes on the requested entity itself, not on nested inventories.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll+0xF6F760 named pseudo-code, lines 54-136 read: HasComponent of DAT_182204020 (OwnerComponent) and DAT_1821f9b28 (IsLockedComponent); precondition EoCServer.dll+0x336480 = HasComponent of DAT_1821f166c (eoc::PlayerComponent); add helper +0xF6F180 (ComponentFrameStorageAllocRaw of IsLockedComponent), remove helper +0xF6F310 (RemoveComponentUnchecked of IsLockedComponent). The names lock/unlock/toggle for 0/1/2 are from this behaviour, not from an enum string.
does.check: not checkable live: no recipe yet (lead): lock a player character's inventory from the inventory UI (the request comes from the client's LEGACY_RequestLockInventories); then {appears: eoc::inventory::IsLockedComponent} on that character on the server, and {gone: eoc::inventory::IsLockedComponent} after unlocking it

does.text: For every entity whose eoc::PlayerComponent was just removed, queues lock change 1 (unlock) for it, so a character that stops being a player's loses IsLockedComponent on the next ProcessLockRequests.
